metadata.title: Council Directive 65/65/EEC on the approximation of provisions laid down by law, regulation or administrative action relating to proprietary medicinal products

candidates.statement: Whereas the primary purpose of any rules concerning the production and distribution of proprietary medicinal products must be to safeguard public health;
candidates.context: Having regard to the Opinion of the Economic and Social Committee (2); Whereas, however, this objective must be attained by means which will not hinder the development of the pharmaceutical industry or trade in medicinal products within the Community;

candidates.statement: Whereas, however, this objective must be attained by means which will not hinder the development of the pharmaceutical industry or trade in medicinal products within the Community;
candidates.context: Whereas the primary purpose of any rules concerning the production and distribution of proprietary medicinal products must be to safeguard public health; Whereas trade in proprietary medicinal products within the Community is hindered by disparities between certain national provisions, in particular between provisions relating to medicinal products (excluding substances or combinations of substances which are foods, animal feeding-stuffs or toilet preparations) ; and whereas such disparities directly affect the establishment and functioning of the common market;

candidates.statement: Whereas such hindrances must accordingly be removed ; and whereas this entails approximation of the relevant provisions;
candidates.context: Whereas trade in proprietary medicinal products within the Community is hindered by disparities between certain national provisions, in particular between provisions relating to medicinal products (excluding substances or combinations of substances which are foods, animal feeding-stuffs or toilet preparations) ; and whereas such disparities directly affect the establishment and functioning of the common market; Whereas, however, such approximation can only be achieved progressively ; and whereas priority must be given to eliminating the disparities liable to have the greatest effect on the functioning of the common market;

candidates.statement: For the purposes of this Directive, the following shall have the meanings hereby assigned to them; 1. Proprietary medicinal product:
candidates.context: Any ready-prepared medicinal product placed on the market under a special name and in a special pack.

candidates.statement: The provisions of Chapters II to V shall apply only to proprietary medicinal products for human use intended to be placed on the market in Member States.
candidates.context: CHAPTER II Authorisation to place proprietary medicinal products on the market

candidates.statement: In order to obtain an authorisation to place a proprietary medicinal product on the market as provided for in Article 3, the person responsible for placing that product on the market shall make application to the competent authority of the Member State concerned.
candidates.context: The application shall be accompanied by the following particulars and documents: 1. Name or corporate name and permanent address of the person responsible for placing the proprietary product on the market and, where applicable, of the manufacturer.

candidates.statement: The application shall be accompanied by the following particulars and documents: 1. Name or corporate name and permanent address of the person responsible for placing the proprietary product on the market and, where applicable, of the manufacturer.
candidates.context: In order to obtain an authorisation to place a proprietary medicinal product on the market as provided for in Article 3, the person responsible for placing that product on the market shall make application to the competent authority of the Member State concerned. 2. Name of the proprietary product (brand name, or common name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer, or scientific name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer).

candidates.statement: The authorisation provided for in Article 3 shall be refused if, after verification of the particulars and documents listed in Article 4, it proves that the proprietary medicinal product is harmful in the normal conditions of use, or that its therapeutic efficacy is lacking or is insufficiently substantiated by the applicant, or that its qualitative and quantitative composition is not as declared.
candidates.context: Authorisation shall likewise be refused if the particulars and documents submitted in support of the application do not comply with Article 4.

candidates.statement: Member States shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that the procedure for granting an authorisation to place a proprietary medicinal product on the market is completed within 120 days of the date of submitting the application.
candidates.context: In exceptional cases this time limit may be extended for a further ninety days. The applicant shall be notified of such extension before the expiry of the initial time limit.

candidates.statement: In exceptional cases this time limit may be extended for a further ninety days. The applicant shall be notified of such extension before the expiry of the initial time limit.
candidates.context: Member States shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that the procedure for granting an authorisation to place a proprietary medicinal product on the market is completed within 120 days of the date of submitting the application.

candidates.statement: Member States shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that the holder of an authorisation furnishes proof that the controls have been carried out on the finished product in accordance with the methods described by the applicant pursuant to item 7 of the second paragraph of Article 4.
Authorisation shall not affect the civil and criminal liability of the manufacturer and, where applicable, of the person responsible for placing the proprietary medicinal product on the market.
Authorisations shall be valid for five years and shall be renewed for five-year periods, on application by the holder within the three months preceding expiry.
candidates.context: CHAPTER III Suspension and revocation of authorisation to market proprietary medicinal products

candidates.statement: The competent authorities of the Member States shall suspend or revoke an authorisation to place a proprietary medicinal product on the market where that product proves to be harmful in the normal conditions of use, or where its therapeutic efficacy is lacking, or where its qualitative and quantitative composition is not as declared. Therapeutic efficacy is lacking when it is established that therapeutic results cannot be obtained with the proprietary product.
candidates.context: An authorisation shall also be suspended or revoked where the particulars supporting the application as provided for in Article 4 are found to be incorrect, or when the controls on the finished product referred to in Article 8 have not been carried out.

candidates.statement: All decisions taken pursuant to Articles 5, 6 or 11 shall state in detail the reasons on which they are based. A decision shall be notified to the party concerned, who shall at the same time be informed of the remedies available to him under the laws in force and of the time limit allowed for the exercise of such remedies.
candidates.context: Authorisations to place a proprietary product on the market and decisions to revoke authorisations shall be published by each Member State in the appropriate official publication.

CHAPTER IV Labelling of proprietary medicinal products

candidates.statement: The following particulars shall appear on containers and outer packages of proprietary medicinal products: 1. Name of the proprietary product which may be a brand name, or a common name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer, or a scientific name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer.
candidates.context: 2. Next to the name of the proprietary product, a statement of the active constituents expressed qualitatively and quantitatively per dose-unit or as a percentage, according to the pharmaceutical form. The international non-proprietary names recommended by the World Health Organisation shall be used wherever they exist.

Next to the name of the proprietary product, a statement of the active constituents expressed qualitatively and quantitatively per dose-unit or as a percentage, according to the pharmaceutical form. The international non-proprietary names recommended by the World Health Organisation shall be used wherever they exist.
candidates.context: The following particulars shall appear on containers and outer packages of proprietary medicinal products: 1. Name of the proprietary product which may be a brand name, or a common name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer, or a scientific name together with a trade mark or name of the manufacturer. 3. Reference number for production identification (manufacturer's batch number).

candidates.statement: In the case of ampoules, the particulars required under the first paragraph of Article 13 shall be given on the outer packages. However, on the actual containers only the following particulars are required: - name of the proprietary medicinal product;
candidates.context: - quantity of active constituents;

candidates.statement: As regards small single-dose containers, other than ampoules, on which it is impossible to give the particulars mentioned in Article 14, the requirements of Article 13 shall apply only to the outer package.
In the case of narcotics, in addition to the particulars mentioned in Article 13, a special sign consisting of a double red line shall appear on both the outer package and the container.
Where there is no outer package, the particulars which should feature on such a package pursuant to the preceding Articles shall be shown on the container.

The particulars mentioned in items, 6, 7 and 8 of the first paragraph of Article 13 shall appear on the outer package and on the container of proprietary medicinal products in the language or languages of the country where they are being placed on the market.
The provisions of this Chapter shall not prevent the particulars required by rules other than those to which this Directive relates from being given on outer packages or on containers.

All decisions taken in pursuance of the preceding paragraph shall state in detail the reasons on which they are based. A decision shall be notified to the party concerned, who shall at the same time be informed of the remedies available to him under the laws in force and of the time limit allowed for the exercise of such remedies.
candidates.context: Where the provisions of this Chapter are not observed and an order addressed to the person concerned has remained without effect, the competent authorities of the Member States may suspend or revoke the authorisation to place the proprietary medicinal product on the market. CHAPTER V General and final provisions

candidates.statement: An authorisation to market a proprietary medicinal product shall not be refused, suspended or revoked except on the grounds set out in this Directive.
Member States shall put into force the measures needed in order to comply with this Directive within eighteen months of its notification and shall inform the Commission forthwith.
Member States shall ensure that they communicate to the Commission the text of the main provisions of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.

In the five years following the notification mentioned in Article 22, the rules for which provision is made in this Directive shall be applied progressively to proprietary medicinal products covered by an authorisation to place on the market by virtue of previous provisions.
